s10-longest-substring-without-repeating-.trick: Remember each character's latest index. If it lies inside the current window, move the left boundary just past it.

s10-max-consecutive-ones-iii.trick: Maintain a window with at most k zeroes. When it has too many, move its left edge until valid again.

s10-fruit-into-baskets.trick: A valid window contains at most two fruit types. Count types in a map and shrink when a third appears.
s10-fruit-into-baskets.space: O(1), at most three types held temporarily

s10-longest-repeating-character-replacem.trick: For uppercase letters, a window is valid when its length minus its most frequent letter count is at most k. Shrink until valid.

s10-binary-subarray-with-sum.trick: For a binary array, count subarrays with sum at most goal, then subtract those with sum at most goal-1.

s10-count-number-of-nice-subarrays.trick: Count windows containing at most k odd values, then subtract those with at most k-1 odds.

s10-number-of-substring-containing-all-t.trick: Track the latest positions of a, b and c. For every right endpoint, all starts up to the earliest of those positions form valid substrings.

s10-maximum-point-you-can-obtain-from-ca.trick: Start with k cards from the left. Repeatedly replace one left card with one from the right and keep the maximum sum.

s10-longest-substring-with-at-most-k-dis.trick: Count characters in the current window. When it contains more than k distinct characters, shrink it from the left.

s10-subarray-with-k-different-integers.trick: Exactly k distinct equals at most k distinct minus at most k-1 distinct. Each at-most count uses a shrinking frequency-map window.

s10-minimum-window-substring.trick: Expand until the window contains every required character (including duplicates), then shrink from the left while preserving that condition.

s10-minimum-window-subsequence.trick: Dynamic programming stores the latest start index of a source prefix matching each prefix of the target as a subsequence. Update target positions backwards per source character.
